cards.action: Manage the number of seats before the token spend. Review token cost only for seats with heavy use.
cards.caveat: The simulated staff are light users. Heavy agent use changes the ratio.
cards.error: none for the counts; the token cost is list price, not a bill
evidence: Licences in the window: 271.43; token cost at list prices: 0.89
Per task started: 4.24 of licence against 0.014 of tokens
Tokens equal the seat price at about 1,702 tasks per seat per month; staff did 2.7 tasks per person per week
cards.finding: Seats cost 304 times the token cost of the work done on them.
cards.title: The cost is in the seats, not in the tokens

cards.action: Make Atlas the default for work that needs company data.
cards.caveat: Every script was run once on every platform. In a company that is a planned test set, not what the traces give for free.
cards.error: sampling interval, 75 checked turns per platform from 32 scripts
evidence: Checked turns correct: Atlas 66/75, Beacon 37/75, Chatly 11/75
Atlas against Beacon: +39 points, 95% interval +24 to +53 with the script as the unit
31 of 64 tasks started on another platform than Atlas
cards.finding: Atlas is right on 88% of checked turns, Beacon on 49% and Chatly on 15%.
cards.readiness_rule: D3 bar: the interval of the difference excludes zero with the script as the unit
cards.title: Atlas gets the most answers right

cards.action: Do not cancel on this evidence. Ask the holders, or wait until the evidence rule fires.
cards.caveat: A holder with one seat is never flagged. A seat used rarely but for something that matters looks the same as an unused one.
evidence: Quiet seats: hana on Chatly (0 of 6 starts), dmitri on Chatly (0 of 6 starts), ines on Beacon (0 of 1 starts), ines on Chatly (0 of 1 starts), freya on Beacon (0 of 3 starts), freya on Chatly (0 of 3 starts), ben on Atlas (0 of 4 starts)
A seat with no start is evidence only after its holder has made 29 task starts. The busiest holder made 9; at the observed rates that takes 4 to 56 more weeks
In a simulation of this company, the 10% share rule flags a seat that is in use in 97% of 2-week windows
Used only as a fallback after a failure elsewhere: dmitri on Chatly
cards.finding: 7 of 24 seats had almost no task starts, worth 150 of 570 per month, and 0 of them can be called unused on this evidence.
cards.readiness_rule: D1 bar: the chance of this few starts at a true share of 10% is under 5%
cards.title: Quiet seats, not yet unused seats

cards.action: Add the MCP server `shop` to Chatly, or send that work to a platform that has it.
cards.caveat: The next platform may have used the capability only because it was there. A capability the first platform has but did not use in the window counts as missing.
cards.error: task links: precision 13/13, recall 13/13; inability phrase scored above
evidence: 3 of 3 tasks that left Chatly used the MCP server shop on the next platform
Tasks started on Chatly that were re-done elsewhere or ended on trouble: 78% (7/9)
8 more tasks ended on Chatly with a reply that says it cannot reach the data; 50% (11/22) of its turns carry such a phrase (the phrase marks a wrong answer in 9 of 10 checked turns)
cards.finding: 11 tasks failed on Chatly, which does not have the MCP server `shop`.
cards.readiness_rule: D4 bar: the same gap in 5 tasks or more is `act`, in 3 or 4 `check first` (here 11)
cards.title: Chatly lacks the MCP server shop

cards.action: Do not rank platforms by error rates. Fund about 30 checked answers per period, and check flagged turns first.
cards.caveat: Failure rates from flagged turns only are biased upwards. Use a random sample for the rate.
evidence: Silent failures: 51% (19/37), 95% interval 36% to 67%
A failed tool call marks a wrong answer in 4 of 18 turns; an inability phrase in 11 of 13
10 checked turns per platform pick the best platform in 96% of simulated samples: 30 checks for the period
cards.finding: 19 of 37 turns that failed a check show no error, no empty reply and no "I can't" in the trace.
cards.readiness_rule: counted against checks; the interval is far from zero
cards.title: Half of the wrong answers leave no sign in the trace

cards.action: Start with Beacon: find what its re-done tasks needed (see the capability cards).
cards.caveat: People time is the length of a session, not effort. Tasks dropped with no sign in the trace are not counted.
cards.error: task links: precision 13/13, recall 13/13; the trouble flag is right for 9 of 19 sessions, so the upper bound is loose
evidence: Re-done sessions: 13 of 77
Upper bound with sessions that ended on trouble: 34% of cost, 28% of time
Highest on Beacon: 28% of its token cost was re-done elsewhere
cards.finding: 13% of the token cost and 8% of people's time went to sessions that the person then re-did on another platform.
cards.readiness_rule: linked evidence with a loose upper bound
cards.title: Work that is done twice

cards.action: Add the skill `weekly-sales-report` to Beacon, or send that work to a platform that has it.
cards.caveat: The next platform may have used the capability only because it was there. A capability the first platform has but did not use in the window counts as missing.
evidence: 3 of 7 tasks that left Beacon used the skill weekly-sales-report on the next platform
Tasks started on Beacon that were re-done elsewhere or ended on trouble: 41% (9/22)
cards.finding: 3 tasks failed on Beacon, which does not have the skill `weekly-sales-report`.
cards.readiness_rule: D4 bar: the same gap in 5 tasks or more is `act`, in 3 or 4 `check first` (here 3)
cards.title: Beacon lacks the skill weekly-sales-report

cards.action: Do not route by task type yet. Plan a test set of 10 checked tasks per platform and task type.
cards.caveat: The simulation takes each cell's observed rate as the true rate. Smaller real gaps need more checks.
cards.error: sampling interval; cells hold 4 to 16 checked turns
evidence: Comparisons significant at 0.05: 9 of 21; after correction for many tests: 7
Task types where another platform has the highest rate: none
10 checks per platform and task type pick the right platform 9 times in 10 on average: 210 checks. The window produced 134 checkable turns and 16 of 21 cells are short of 10
cards.finding: 7 of 21 platform comparisons inside a task type hold up, and no task type has a clear best platform other than Atlas.
cards.readiness_rule: D3 bar not met inside task types
cards.title: Not enough checks to route by task type

cards.action: Show the work map by domain only, and only for platforms whose labels agree. Fix the task type label before it is used across platforms.
cards.caveat: The chat platform's transcripts have no tool lines, so the same work reads differently. Labels come from many small free models.
evidence: Agreement between platforms (kappa): domain 0.44 to 0.85, task type 0.31 to 0.59
Label equals the designed label: Atlas domain 88% (28/32), task type 66% (21/32), Beacon domain 78% (25/32), task type 59% (19/32), Chatly domain 69% (22/32), task type 50% (16/32)
The smallest role has 4 people; the minimum group size is 5
cards.finding: The same task gets the same task type on all three platforms in 34% (11/32) of scripts.
cards.readiness_rule: D2 bar: kappa 0.6 or more, and groups at or above the minimum size
cards.title: The work map cannot be compared across platforms yet
